## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? --- I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of. Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does. Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable Android-friendly Commandos-style stealth tactics game, or adapt the existing game.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Build a standalone, procedural isometric game titled “Commandos: Realist — Operation Nightfall.”
- Use a canvas renderer with touch controls, stealth/combat mechanics, mission objectives, and responsive HUD.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added the game’s HTML structure, start screen, HUD, help/pause/end overlays, and touch-control UI.
- Added responsive visual styling for mobile and desktop.
- Implemented procedural audio and world generation/terrain rendering foundations.

### Active
- Continue implementing the actual renderer, soldiers, enemy AI, controls, mission logic, and game loop.
- Test gameplay and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `src/game.js` and continue after `World.renderTerrain()`.
2. Implement drawing, unit behavior, touch/keyboard input, objectives, and complete game lifecycle.
3. Run the app, verify it is playable, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, HUD, overlays, and script entry point.
- `styles.css`: Responsive game and interface styling.
- `src/game.js`: Procedural audio and world/terrain foundations; game implementation is incomplete.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `index.html` loads `src/game.js` as a module, but `src/game.js` currently ends after `World.renderTerrain()`; no complete game loop or gameplay has been implemented yet.

11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.

13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.

15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.

22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.

- Build a complete, playable Android-friendly Commandos-style stealth tactics game by adapting the existing project.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

- Build a standalone procedural isometric game titled “Commandos: Realist — Operation Nightfall.”
- Use a canvas renderer with touch controls, stealth/combat mechanics, mission objectives, and a responsive HUD.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game UI structure, responsive styling, procedural audio, and world/terrain generation foundations.
- Added initial game framework in `src/game.js`, including unit/guard setup, input binding, camera transforms, movement pathfinding, squad selection, crouch/hold controls, and preliminary knife/grenade actions.

- (none)

- `src/game.js`: Procedural audio/world plus the incomplete game implementation.
- `index.html`: Game UI, HUD, overlays, touch controls, and module entry point.
- `styles.css`: Responsive game and interface styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The generated map contains a coastal compound, buildings, searchlights, props, and extraction/insertion markers.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Complete the existing project as a playable Android-friendly Commandos-style stealth tactics game.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Build a standalone procedural isometric game titled “Commandos: Realist — Operation Nightfall.”
- Use canvas rendering with touch controls, stealth/combat mechanics, mission objectives, and a responsive HUD.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game UI, responsive styling, procedural audio, world and terrain generation, and core squad, guard, movement, pathfinding, combat, interaction, objective, and HUD systems.
- Inspected controls, drawing helpers, world setup, objective locations, and the incomplete `Game` class and HTML controls.

### Active
- Finish `src/game.js` with scene rendering, minimap, keyboard controls, animation frame loop, module initialization, and closing braces.
- Verify objective interactions and win/loss lifecycle; play-test and fix runtime issues.
- Capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `src/game.js` ends inside `Game` after `updateHUD()`; `node --check src/game.js` fails with `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input`.

## Next Move
1. Implement rendering, `drawMinimap()`, keyboard input, and `frame()` in `src/game.js`; close and initialize the module.
2. Run syntax checks, launch and play-test, then fix gameplay or UI issues found.
3. Capture a viewport ≤1280px JPEG and inspect only that latest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Incomplete game implementation, ending after `updateHUD()`.
- `index.html`: HUD, controls, overlays, and module entry point.
- `styles.css`: Responsive game and interface styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: App launch helper.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Map includes a coastal compound, buildings, searchlights, props, insertion/extraction markers, and 12 guards.
- Objectives: recover battle plans, destroy the radio tower, extract the squad; freeing the prisoner is optional.
- The start screen initially overlays the canvas; `start()` hides it by adding `hidden`.

## Objective
- Complete the existing project as a playable Android-friendly Commandos-style stealth tactics game.
- Verify gameplay, capture a small JPEG screenshot, and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Keep visual-check screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Build a standalone procedural isometric game titled “Commandos: Realist — Operation Nightfall.”
- Use canvas rendering with touch controls, stealth/combat mechanics, mission objectives, and a responsive HUD.

## Work State

### Completed
- Added game UI, responsive styling, procedural audio, world and terrain generation, and core squad, guard, movement, pathfinding, combat, interaction, objective, and HUD systems.

### Active
- Finish `src/game.js` with rendering, `drawMinimap()`, keyboard controls, `frame()`, module initialization, and closing braces.
- Verify objective interactions and win/loss lifecycle; play-test and fix runtime issues.
- Capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `src/game.js` ends inside `Game.updateHUD()` at line 941 with no class/module closure; syntax check previously failed with `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input`.
- `frame()`, `drawMinimap()`, and `keyDown()` are referenced but not implemented.

## Next Move
1. Implement rendering, minimap, keyboard input, and animation frame loop in `src/game.js`; close and initialize the module.
2. Run syntax checks, launch and play-test, then fix gameplay or UI issues found.
3. Capture a viewport ≤1280px JPEG and inspect only that latest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Incomplete game implementation, ending after `updateHUD()`.
- `index.html`: HUD, controls, overlays, and module entry point.
- `styles.css`: Responsive game and interface styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: App launch helper.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Map includes a coastal compound, buildings, searchlights, props, insertion/extraction markers, and 12 guards.
- Objectives: recover battle plans, destroy the radio tower, extract the squad; freeing the prisoner is optional.
- The start screen overlays the canvas; `start()` hides it by adding `hidden`.
